recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up source edit is needed unless MnM separately chooses to make editorial improvements to the existing explanatory prose.
issue_request: FHIR-13476 was a Published/Persuasive non-substantive correction for the FHIR core datatypes HumanName examples. The reporter said an example appeared to suggest a Given Name use of Common, but HumanName.use has no Common option; the relevant example/guidance needed to use nickname-related NameUse semantics instead.
initial_application: Jira records svn revision 12451 as the application. Git-svn commit 2b98f3b9f478f79e068e0d4fc14ee5af57cc9c95 is that revision and added HumanName usual-versus-nickname discussion plus a concrete nickname example to source/datatypes-examples.html. The commit subject cites #13746, but FHIR-13746 is a separate Quantity-link correction at adjacent svn revision 12450, so this appears to be a historical commit-message typo rather than a source mismatch.
additional_context: The current HumanName spreadsheet source lists NameUse as usual, official, temp, nickname, anonymous, old, and maiden, with no Common code. The current datatypes examples page is linked from the datatypes page and preserves examples using use="usual" for everyday/preferred names, a separate XML and JSON nickname example using use="nickname", and explanatory text about the ambiguity between usual and nickname. Direct FHIR-13476 Zulip and Confluence-reference searches found no conflicting community evidence.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. An exact source search found no remaining HumanName example that uses Common/common as HumanName.use, and the source already conveys the corrected usage.

related_jiras.note: The historical git-svn commit subject appears to typo this adjacent key, but FHIR-13746 itself is an unrelated Published Quantity-link issue at svn revision 12450 and was not decided here.
